question.leadin: This ruler bore Caesarion while serving as Julius Caesar's mistress.
question.text: Who is this female Egyptian pharaoh from the Ptolemy dynasty who notably killed herself with a snakebite?
question.clue: This ruler allegedly won a bet by drinking pearls dissolved in vinegar, and while besieged by enemies, this monarch asked for and received a basket of figs.

swap.leadin: In the aftermath of this battle, the earliest known surviving peace treaty was signed by Hattusili III.
swap.text: Name this battle dated to 1274 BC and fought between the New Kingdom of Egypt and the Hittites in a namesake city on the Orontes River in present-day Syria.
swap.clue: The opposing leader declared victory in the success of his empire's technological advances in matching those of the opposing Hittites.

question.text: This young pharaoh, the son of Akhenaten, had his tomb excavated by Howard Carter.
question.clue: George Herbert financed a mission in the Valley of the Kings that stumbled upon the resting place of this Pharaoh, son of Akhenaten.

swap.text: The discovery of this pharaoh's tomb was monumental because it was nearly fully intact, with very few artifacts stolen by grave robbers. Howard Carter discovered the tomb of this pharaoh, the youngest ruler of Egypt.
swap.clue: This pharaoh moved Egypt's capital back to Thebes from Amarna and reinstated the worship of traditional Egyptian gods.

question.text: This pharaoh of the Third Dynasty is most well-known for building a Step Pyramid at Saqqara, which was the first large fully stone building in Egypt. He also subdued the Sinai.
question.clue: An official of this pharaoh communes with the god Khnum to stop a seven-year flood, as recorded on the Famine Stela.

swap.text: In addition to the Spartans, belligerents from Thespiae and this city were present at the last stand. This city's Sacred Band was an elite military unit composed of gay lovers.
swap.clue: Troops from this city employed the "cutting off the snake's head" technique to defeat Cleombrotus of Sparta.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Old Kingdom pharaohs.
question.text: Name this pharaoh who unified Upper and Lower Egypt and is depicted on a namesake palette wearing the crowns of both parts. Alternatively, name the legendary unifier of Egypt who is often identified with him.
question.clue: This founder of the First Dynasty depicted on a namesake "Palette" who unified Upper and Lower Egypt.

swap.text: Ships traveling long distances in the ancient world stopped at the Himyarite site of Muza on this body of water. The Aksumite kingdom also used their papyrus-sailed ships to guard ports on this sea.
swap.clue: The kingdoms of Saba' and Himyar exported frankincense and myrrh ("murr") to the Roman Empire through this sea, whose western coastline was also home to the kingdom of Axum.

question.text: The Story of Sinuhe ("sin-NOO-hay") references the murder of Amenemhat I, a ruler of this Egyptian kingdom that ruled between the first two Intermediate Periods.
question.clue: The fnal rulers of this period were called the Xois Dynasty since they moved the capital there.

swap.text: This pharaoh commanded the Egyptian forces at Kadesh. The temples at Abu Simbel were built during his reign.
swap.clue: In 1976, this ruler's remains were flown to Paris, where they were received with the full honors of a foreign dignitary.

question.leadin: The last inscription in this writing system is the Graffito of Esmet-Akhom in the late 4th Century CE.
question.text: Name this script. Jean-Francois Champollion used the Rosetta Stone to decipher this form of writing, which was included on the stone along with Greek and Demotic.

swap.text: Aksumite rulers were known for constructing monuments of this type, consisting of tapered pillars with a pyramidal top. Many Egyptian monuments of this type, such as ones named "Lateran" and "Vatican," were installed in Rome under the Roman Empire.
swap.clue: One of these structures built by Aksum was cut into three pieces for transport to Italy before being repatriated in 2005. A pair of these objects named for Cleopatra are found in London and New York City.

question.text: This group is often credited with introducing chariot warfare to ancient Egypt. This group ruled over the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt from the city of Avaris.
question.clue: Their capital was at Avaris, and they were overthrown by Ahmose.

swap.text: The Armana letters were written during this period of ancient Egyptian history. This period followed the second intermediate period and marked Egypt at the height of its power.
swap.clue: The first ruler of it was known as the "son of the moon-god Iah" and erected the Tempest Stele and Donation Stele.

question.leadin: Researchers determined that a "screaming mummy" discovered next to the body of a pharaoh of this name was his son Pentawere, who had been forced to hang himself over his role in an assassination plot.
question.text: Give this name of the pharaoh targeted by Pentawere's mother, Tiye, in the "harem conspiracy." An earlier pharaoh with this name commissioned the temples at Abu Simbel ("AH-boo SEEM-bel") and won the Battle of Kadesh ("kah-DESH").
question.answerHtml: Ramesses [ accept Ramesses the Great or Ramesses II; accept Ramesses III; accept Ramses in place of “Ramesses”; prompt on Ozymandias]
question.clue: An earlier ruler with this name fought a battle on the Orontes River against the forces of Muwatalli II, which is depicted in sculptures at the Abu Simbel complex.

swap.text: Menander's plays are among the roughly half a million papyri unearthed at this Egyptian site, which is named for a "sharp-nosed fish."
swap.clue: Many of the finds from the excavation at this site led by Grenfell and Hunt are housed in the Sackler Library in Oxford.

question.leadin: The second story in this text is about a man who fashions a wax crocodile, which comes to life on contact with water, and eats the man who slept with his wife.
question.text: Name this ancient document discovered by a namesake British explorer, which consists of five tales about magicians. In another of its stories, the heroine Rededjet gives birth to three future kings, by the prophecy of Dedi.

swap.leadin: Seti I fought a war against these people, whom he called the "Tjehnu," and the Great Karnak Inscription describes the defeat of their "Great Chief" Meryey's alliance with the Lukka and four Sea Peoples.
swap.text: Name this people, who at one point ruled Egypt in a dynasty descended from Osorkon the Elder. A stele recounting one pharaoh's victory over these people is also one of the first documents to mention the word "Israel."

question.leadin: This woman invented an early double-boiler, now culinarily referred to as this woman's namesake bath.
question.text: Identify this first-century woman, who Zosimos of Panopolis regarded as the first alchemist in the Western world. She is known for a namesake alchemical axiom stating "One becomes two, two becomes three, and out of the third comes the one as the fourth."
question.answerHtml: Mary the Jewess [accept Mary the Prophetess; accept Maria the Copt; accept Maria Hebraea; accept Maria Prophetissa; accept Māriyya al-Qibṭiyya; prompt on Mary alone]

swap.leadin: Critics of this historian claim that he has mis-interpreted a Ugaritic inscription to date a solar eclipse during the reign of Akhenaten to 1012 B.C.E, 350 years later than the conventional dating scheme.
swap.text: Name this Egyptologist and former rock musician who, in the book A Test of Time, put forth a highly controversial New Chronology which shifts the reigns of dozens of pharaohs forward by centuries.
